meta.title: Redaura — alert infrastructure for harm reduction
hero.sub: Redaura lets drug-checking and harm-reduction organizations send a warning to every phone in a defined area, in seconds, in the reader's own language, credited to their organization by name.
hero.pushBody: Near you: pills sold as MDMA contain PMMA. Alert by Unity · Jellinek.
stats.l1: From approval to phones in the area
gap.p1: A drug-checking team finds a mislabelled sample at a festival at 1am. They have the result, the equipment, and twenty years of trust with the people at that festival. Their only way to spread the warning is a whiteboard outside the tent and a post that reaches whoever is already following them.
gap.p2: National monitoring systems have the reach, but not this mandate. They aggregate, they track trends, they issue guidance over weeks. They were never built to put a warning on thirty thousand phones tonight.
gap.heading: Redaura connects the two.
feat1.title: Only vetted organizations publish
feat1.copy: Accreditation happens before an account exists. A volunteer at the testing point drafts the alert; a designated lead releases it. Two people, every time.
feat2.title: Structured alerts, not free text
feat2.copy: Alerts are built from fixed fields, not written as prose. Every value is expert-reviewed in 20+ languages, so a Dutch team's warning arrives natively in Polish or German with no translation step and no room for slang or ambiguity.
feat3.title: Nobody is tracked
feat3.copy: Matching happens on the device — the phone works out whether it's inside an alert area. Nothing is transmitted, nothing is logged, nothing can be subpoenaed. That's the architecture, not a setting.
feat4.title: The data goes both ways
feat4.copy: Because alerts are structured, the same publication that reaches phones tonight can reach national monitoring tonight, in a format their systems already read. The publisher decides what goes where.
app.title: One app.
app.note1: Users download a single global client; the alerts on it belong to the organizations that publish them — their name, their logo, their lab reference. The trust built on the ground travels with the warning.
app.note2: Tap an alert to open it. A push lands a few seconds later, or replay it under the phone.
quote.text: “We have the volunteers, the test kits, and twenty years of trust. What we never had was €50,000 for an app.”
quote.attr: — Drug checking coordinator, prospective pilot partner
pilot.title: Working prototype. Open protocol.
pilot.note:
A non-profit registered in the Netherlands, built and hosted in the EU. We're looking for three founding partners — drug-checking services, peer-support networks, or regional health bodies — to shape this before it ships. Pilot partners sit on the governance board and set the accreditation rules.

A one-page letter of intent is all we need. Non-binding, no funding commitment, no exclusivity.
pilot.name: Name
pilot.done: Received. We'll reply within two days — from a human.
pilot.follow: Not an organization but want to follow along? Leave an email — updates roughly monthly.
